rationale: Treesort is a tiny pointer- and recursion-heavy benchmark (tree insertion, key comparisons, in-order traversal) with almost no global state or indirect call sites, so IGV and ICALL are omitted as they would find few targets and add only noise. SUB is weighted toward high security/diversity gain with low cost and risk weights because algebraic instruction substitution is nearly free and safe, making it ideal for the many comparison and arithmetic operations. IBR gets strong security weight with moderate cost sensitivity since indirect branching meaningfully disrupts the traversal control-flow graph at acceptable overhead. BCF has the highest security weight but equally high RuntimeCost/SizeCost weights so the optimizer only applies it where the security payoff justifies its large code and runtime inflation — important for a program whose tree operations are on the hot path. FLA receives moderate security weight with elevated RuntimeCost and CorrectnessRisk weights because flattening interacts poorly with recursive, pointer-driven code where restructuring errors or register pressure could harm both correctness and performance. SPLIT is kept cheap and low-risk, serving as a diversity amplifier that composes well with FLA and BCF without meaningful overhead.
